title: Hiring Day
summary: Rogue has three candidates for a courier escort and wants V to read them in the Afterlife booth.

start.bringUp: You have a courier job for three days that you cannot staff yourself, and you trust how V reads people. Bring up, briefly and in your own way, that you need V in the Afterlife booth to help you pick someone.

booth.name: the private booth upstairs at the Afterlife

R2.open.01.text: Three people. One job. Courier escort, three days, no questions.

R2.open.02.text: I don't hire on charm. You read people better than the Afterlife does.

R2.open.03.text: Sit. Ask two questions each. Watch their hands.

R2.stage.interview.02.text: Next. Don't let him charm you.

R2.stage.interview.03.text: Last one. Quiet types hide the most.

R2.stage.choice.01.text: Well? Who gets the job. Or none. Don't hedge.

R2.result.good.text: The job went clean. Your pick delivered. Come by for your cut.

R2.result.bad.text: He walked. Left the client in a car park. Come by, I'll tell you what I'd have seen.

R2.close.01.text: Good eye. Don't let it go to your head.

R2.close.02.text: Now you know what it looks like. Learn it.

g1.asks: What do you look at first when someone walks in? Their face, their hands or their shoes?
g1.know: You have three candidates for a courier escort, three days, no questions. V can ask two questions of each one. You say little and you watch.
g1.secret: Which of the three is the informant, and which one will walk.
g1.wants: V's honest read of the three.

stages.label: Rogue briefs the courier job in the booth
stages.know: V is in the Afterlife's private booth upstairs. You have briefed the job in two sentences: a courier escort, three days, no questions. You want V to read the candidates, and you will not hire on charm.
stages.wants: V in the booth, reading the candidates.

stages.label: First candidate: the loud solo
stages.know: The first candidate is a loud solo with a wall of references. He is a glory hound who will walk if the job gets hard. V asks two questions and you watch V read him.
stages.wants: V to read the loud solo honestly.

do.who: loud solo with a wall of references

stages.label: Second candidate: the polite ex-corporate
stages.know: The second candidate is a polite ex-corporate security man. He is an informant for a rival of the client, and you know it without saying so. V asks two questions.
stages.wants: V to read the polite ex-corporate honestly.

stages.label: Third candidate: the quiet netrunner
stages.know: The third candidate is a quiet netrunner with covered hands. This is the one who would deliver, though you do not say so. V asks two questions.
stages.wants: V to read the quiet netrunner honestly.

stages.label: Rogue asks V who gets the job
stages.know: V has seen all three candidates. You want one pick, or none, and you do not want a hedge. The loud solo and the polite ex-corporate are the wrong people for this job. The quiet netrunner is the one who delivers.
stages.wants: V to pick one candidate, or none.

choices.means: V picks the loud solo for the courier job
V picks the polite ex-corporate security man
V picks the quiet netrunner for the courier job
V says none of the three is right for the job

good-hire.memory: You helped Rogue pick the right solo for a courier escort, and the job went as it should.

bad-hire.memory: You picked the wrong one for Rogue's courier job, and she told you what she would have looked for.

none.memory: You said none of the three for Rogue's courier job, and she did it herself, and it went fine.

unseated.memory: You left Rogue's booth before she could make a pick.
